products.name: Lovo (Genny)
products.note: Voice cloning and synthesis; likeness consent; commercial voiceover; synthetic media disclosure

reading.body:
Lovo is a voice cloning and synthesis company whose only listed product, Genny, is built around likeness consent and synthetic media disclosure.

The data covers one product in one category, Voice and Audio. It names no models, no training compute, no data centers, and no power contracts. Nothing here ties Lovo to the grid, to buildings, or to the compute supply chain that constrains AI scaling. The consent and disclosure notes describe how the output is governed, not how it is produced.

That gap is the useful part. Voice synthesis is an inference workload, and inference runs on the same accelerators and the same electricity as everything else. A company in this category inherits the binding constraint without appearing in any of the numbers that describe it. The absence of compute detail is not evidence of small footprint, only of what this record tracks.

What the data does not tell the reader: how much compute Lovo uses, where it runs, what it pays for power, or how large it is. It also does not establish any relationship between Lovo and the unrelated companion product listed under its MCP entry. Treat this as a company identity record, not a measure of scale.
